runs.answer: Inflation means things slowly cost more money over time. Your grandma might have bought candy for a penny when she was little. Today that same candy might cost a dollar. Your money buys less candy than it used to, even though it's still the same money.

Inflation means prices go up over time. Imagine a candy bar costs $1 today. If inflation happens, next year it might cost $1.05. Your money buys a little less candy than it did before. That's inflation: the same money gets you fewer things.

runs.answer:
- Inflation means prices slowly go up over time, so the same amount of money buys less stuff than it used to. A candy bar that cost 50 cents might cost 75 cents years later.

- It usually happens when lots of people want to buy things, but there isn't quite enough to go around. Sellers can charge more because buyers are still willing to pay.

- Your money doesn't disappear, but it can shrink in what it can buy. That's why people often save money in ways that can grow, like a bank account that pays interest.

- Inflation means prices slowly go up over time, so the same amount of money buys a little less than it used to. A candy bar that cost 50 cents when your grandparents were young might cost a dollar or more now.

- It usually happens because more people want to buy things than there are things to sell, or because making things costs more, and stores pass that cost along to shoppers.

- Your money isn't gone when inflation happens, but each dollar can buy less, which is why saving money in a jar under your bed can slowly lose its buying power.
